title: AI-first support troubleshooting
question: What could happen if an AI assistant handles initial troubleshooting before a customer reaches a human support engineer?

quote.text: The support director owns the budget and reports to the chief operating officer, and the head of product relies on tickets as a source of bug reports.

participants.name: Support engineers

quote.text: Support engineers want to keep the interesting cases and worry that they would have to undo wrong steps given by the assistant.

participants.rationale: Take over cases from the assistant.

quote.text: Thirty-eight support engineers work across three time zones, and a tier-two team of eleven handles escalations and works with product engineers on defects.
Team leads ask how handling time and quality would be measured when part of the work is invisible to them.

participants.name: Administrators at larger customers

quote.text: Administrators at larger customers say they want a route to a person that is easy to find.

participants.rationale: Want a route to a person.

quote.text: Premium and enterprise customers have response-time commitments and a named customer success manager.
The legal and privacy team asks where transcripts are stored and whether customers paste credentials or personal data into chat.
Security reviewers want a way to remove tokens from stored transcripts.
Knowledge-base authors point out that out-of-date articles would be repeated at scale.

participants.name: Reseller partner

quote.text: A reseller partner that provides first-line support for its own clients asks whether it would still be needed.

participants.rationale: Provides first-line support for its own clients.

quote.text: Two competitors advertise instant answers from an assistant on their websites, and a few customers have mentioned this on renewal calls.

participants.name: Head of product

quote.text: The support director owns the budget and reports to the chief operating officer, and the head of product relies on tickets as a source of bug reports.

participants.rationale: Relies on tickets for bug reports.

quote.text: An employee representative asked how performance measures for engineers would treat cases the assistant handled first.

participants.name: Customers who give up and never open a case

quote.text: There is no data on customers who are not helped by the assistant and give up, because they never open a case.

participants.name: Customers who write in languages other than English

quote.text: No data exists for languages other than English.

participants.rationale: A fifth of cases, never trialled.

participants.name: Customers who use screen readers

quote.text: The chat window has not been tested with screen readers, and the assistant was trialled in English only, although about a fifth of cases arrive in other languages.

participants.rationale: The chat window was not tested with them.

constraints.quote: The privacy lead notes that chat transcripts are personal data, that retention rules for assistant conversations are not yet defined, and that regulators in some regions may ask how customers are told they are talking to an automated system.
Customers in regulated sectors may need to know when an automated system is involved, and the compliance team has not yet read the relevant guidance.
Security reviewers want a way to remove tokens from stored transcripts.
Premium and enterprise customers have response-time commitments and a named customer success manager.
Success measures, escalation rules and the budget for the assistant have not been set.
The chat window has not been tested with screen readers, and the assistant was trialled in English only, although about a fifth of cases arrive in other languages.
constraints.rationale: An untested accessibility and language need.

constraints.quote: Administrators at three larger customers asked in writing that a route to a person be visible on the first screen.
Reopen rates for the cases the assistant resolved were not tracked.

gap.removeText: The chat window has not been tested with screen readers, and the assistant was trialled in English only, although about a fifth of cases arrive in other languages.
gap.rationale: The only statement about screen readers and language.

alternatives.rationale: Suggestions for the engineer instead of the customer.

claims.statement: 44% of cases were closed at first touch, without escalation.
In the pilot the assistant resolved 34% of the 1,900 cases without a human.
A supplier's case study shows that assistant-first rollouts raise customer satisfaction.
claims.rationale: The case study says so but gives no method and the supplier sells the software.

claims.statement: The assistant improved renewal rates in the pilot.
claims.rationale: There is no evidence on renewal.

claims.statement: The assistant works well in languages other than English.
claims.rationale: It was trialled in English only.
